Pushkar has the postcard shot — ghats, temple skyline, golden light on water. We got it. It took a few seconds and we put the phones away.

From the hilltop, all of Pushkar fits in one frame — the lake at the center, temples around it, hills closing the circle. The whole trip, walkable.

A market walk turned into a long stretch in a decor shop none of us needed anything from. We left with a mirror selfie and no purchases.

mistakenlyhuman I planned this trip like a dataset. Best light for photos, ghat timings, the one sunset shot everyone tells you to get in Pushkar. I got it in a few seconds. I've spent ten years finding patterns in numbers, so I notice when the pattern breaks. On this trip it broke almost immediately — the moments I kept coming back to weren't the ones I'd researched. They were the koi taking bread from my hand. A musician nobody photographed. A shop we spent a long stretch in and bought nothing from. None of that was on the itinerary. That's probably why it stayed. I still make the itinerary — noticing a habit doesn't kill it. Tell me the part of your last trip you didn't plan for and loved anyway.
